experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: fsqrt.d $f0, $f0; fsqrt.d $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 4607182418800017408; movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'fsqrt.d $f0, $f0; fsqrt.d $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency: 8 cycles for 0/Inf/NaN/negative; 10 for exact squares 1, 4, 0.25 and minnorm; 36 for general non-square inputs; 37 for maxsub. Measured with an integer-bit reset chain; 5 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. The sample experiment uses 1.0.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: fsqrt.d $f0, $f8; fsqrt.d $f1, $f9; fsqrt.d $f2, $f10; fsqrt.d $f3, $f11; fsqrt.d $f4, $f12; fsqrt.d $f5, $f13; fsqrt.d $f6, $f14; fsqrt.d $f7, $f15
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f8, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f9, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f10, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f11, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f12, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f13, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f14, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f15, $r4' --asm 'fsqrt.d $f0, $f8; fsqrt.d $f1, $f9; fsqrt.d $f2, $f10; fsqrt.d $f3, $f11; fsqrt.d $f4, $f12; fsqrt.d $f5, $f13; fsqrt.d $f6, $f14; fsqrt.d $f7, $f15'
throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput: CPI 4.5 for special values; 5.5 for exact squares; 18.5 for general inputs; 19.0 for maxsub; 6.0 for minsub. Throughput is initiation-interval bound.

notes: Latency model, fitted and validated on this core with a two-copy chain (the stored experiment runs the operation twice, subtracts the 6-cycle closure and divides by 2). Classes: 8 cycles for special operands (0, Inf, NaN), 10 cycles for the exact / power-of-two path (the stored sample uses 1.0), 36 cycles for a general operand. For 32-bit lanes the vector latency equals 2 x the scalar latency - 5, because the 32-bit lanes make two passes over the 64-bit datapath and share the setup/rounding. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers exactly and run in parallel, only the slowest lane matters. Cross-check with LA664: the square-root/reciprocal-square-root pipeline is exactly one cycle shorter here per datapath pass (LA664 reaches 37 for the general case where LA464 stops one cycle earlier; the 32-bit vector variants shorten by two cycles because they make two passes). The divide and reciprocal pipelines are identical on both cores, and the special/exact classes match exactly.
